subject: Post-demo: FluxHealth perf targets & GPU shortlist — next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@fluxhealth.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FluxHealth perf targets & GPU shortlist — next steps
Attachments: fluxhealth_bench-plan.pdf (application/pdf), fluxhealth_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the detailed walkthrough of the live triage flow and the traffic profiles. I captured the performance constraints we discussed and sketched a short validation plan you can review (attached). Top points from our call: 

- Target SLOs (as discussed):
  • Streaming (live triage): end-to-end p95 token latency target <= 200 ms for the agent-facing stream; p50 <= 80 ms.
  • Non-streaming batch inference (daily summaries): p95 <= 800 ms.
  • Concurrent active sessions target: 120 concurrent streaming sessions during peak; ~1,000 non-concurrent batch requests per hour.
  • Median token output length per streaming session: ~120 tokens (typical turn).

- Workload characteristics we should validate:
  • Many short, streaming requests with small token bursts; KV-cache hit rate expected to be high for repeated context.
  • Mixture of low-latency small-turn exchanges and occasional longer-generation follow-ups.

- Suggested GPU shortlist for Dedicated pilot (initial throughput/cost trade study):
  1) H100 80GB (low-latency, best for large models and high concurrency)
  2) A100 80GB (solid baseline, predictable throughput)
  3) L4 / 48GB-ish inference cards (cost-efficient for quantized variants; fallback tier)

- Pilot proposal (2-week smoke + 2-week validation):
  • Smoke (3 days): verify baseline latency with a small synthetic stream workload (50 concurrent streams).
  • Validation (13 days): run realistic traffic replay (we'll use your sample traces) across the three HW configs, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and concurrency headroom.
  • Acceptance gate: p95 streaming latency <= 200 ms on production-like traffic on at least one HW config with an acceptable cost profile.

Next steps I propose:
1) You approve the pilot scope in the attached mutual action plan (sheet tab: "Pilot scope").
2) We provision a short Dedicated pilot environment (Redwood Dedicated) for three HW profiles and provide test endpoints.
3) Redwood runs the replay tests and shares the benchmark dashboard + raw results.
4) We review findings and pick the production-reserved throughput target and HW commit level.

Cost / billing note: I included a ballpark cost column in the attached mutual action plan. We will refine after the first smoke test.

If that plan looks good, can we lock the pilot start window for next Monday (26 Oct)? If not, give me a suitable date and Ben / Karthik and I will align resources.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

On behalf of Redwood — attachments: fluxhealth_bench-plan.pdf, fluxhealth_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@fluxhealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@fluxhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FluxHealth perf targets & GPU shortlist — next steps

Thanks Mina — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side before we commit to the pilot start date: 

1) Our main worry is tail latency for the live triage stream. The 200 ms p95 you noted is our end-to-end target (including network + client). Can Redwood isolate server-side p95 so we can see how much headroom to budget for network variance?

2) Cost sensitivity: we need a rough delta between H100 and A100 on a per-month reserved basis for the throughput needed to support 120 concurrent sessions. A high-level monthly estimate is fine — we understand this will be refined after the smoke run.

3) Fallback behavior: if the H100 config still misses p95 during peak, can Redwood automatically route to a smaller quantized variant (lower-cost) with graceful degradation? If so, what are the implications for coherence (model outputs may differ)?

If you can answer those three items and confirm whether Oct 26 works, we can sign off on the mutual action plan and share a sanitized trace for the replay.

—Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Product, FluxHealth
sarah@fluxhealth.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@fluxhealth.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@fluxhealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FluxHealth perf targets & GPU shortlist — next steps

Quick answers that we can use to reply to Sarah: 

1) Server-side isolation: yes — our test harness will report server-only latencies (service + model inference). We typically show both server-only and end-to-end (including a network emulation) so you can see the delta. Expect server-side p95 target to be ~120–160 ms on H100 for the models we demo (depends on seq length and batching).

2) Rough cost delta (monthly reserved estimate for target throughput ~120 concurrent streaming sessions):
   • H100 reserved slab: approx $XXk–$YYk/month (we'll attach an initial estimate).
   • A100 reserved slab: approx $~(0.7–0.85x H100) depending on provider pricing and utilization.
   • L4 tier: ~0.2–0.35x of H100 for quantized variants but will require model conversion and may increase tail latency for some patterns.

   I'll drop a clean spreadsheet with the ranges (see attached: internal_cost_estimate_v1.xlsx). Those are conservative placeholders; we'll firm numbers after the smoke test.

3) Fallbacks: Redwood supports policy-based routing — you can configure automatic fallback to a quantized or smaller variant when latency or capacity thresholds trigger. We recommend an A/B style rollout for correctness: route a small fraction of traffic to the quantized variant first, monitor quality metrics (regen rate, hallucination rate on your eval set) and then increase traffic. Note: coherence may vary; we'll include the evals in the pilot to quantify the delta.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions & Sales Engineering
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FluxHealth perf targets & GPU shortlist — next steps

Thanks Sarah — great questions. Short answers and concrete next steps below, plus I updated the MPA to reflect the Oct 26 start option.

Server-side isolation: we will provide a server-only latency report (p50/p95/p99) and a separate end-to-end run with network emulation. For planning assume server p95 target ~140 ms on H100 for your median turn lengths; we'll measure precisely in the smoke run.

Cost delta: Ben attached a placeholder estimate (internal_cost_estimate_v1.xlsx). We'll confirm after smoke.

Fallbacks and coherence: Redwood can do automatic fallback to a quantized variant. Our recommendation for FluxHealth pilot:
  • Primary: H100 profile running the full-precision model for critical routing (aim for p95 <=200ms end-to-end).
  • Secondary: quantized A100/L4 variant as the automatic overflow/fallback with canary routing (start at 5% of traffic).
  • Eval hooks: we will run regeneration/quality checks on a prompt subset you provide; if coherence drops beyond a preset threshold we will increase capacity or alter routing.

Proposed immediate actions:
  1) FluxHealth: please sign the attached mutual_action_plan.xlsx (tab: "Pilot scope") and upload the sanitized trace to the Drive folder in the link above.
  2) Redwood: provision smoke endpoints (3 HW profiles) and share test endpoint/credentials by COB Wed (21 Oct).
  3) Joint: 30-min sync on Oct 26 to kick off the smoke and agree on the acceptance gate — I can host at 10:00 PT if that works for your team.

I'll follow up with calendar invites and a short pilot-readiness checklist once we have the signed MPA. Opening the HubSpot deal now (FLX-2026-087).

Cheers —
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
